  • 深入回顧2006年台灣政局關鍵轉折，剖析民進黨如何因高捷案與第一家庭弊案陷入空前危機。
  • 解析國民黨在馬英九帶領下如日中天的氣勢，以及黨內接班台北市長的激烈初選角逐背景。
  • 揭示親民黨主席宋楚瑜在大選失利後的政治困境，以及國親兩黨面臨整併與生存的權力博弈。

摘要

政治風暴的前奏：高捷弊案重創綠營執政

作者回顧2006年台北市長選舉前夕的台灣政局，指出當時選民焦點並非市政，而是圍繞在時任總統陳水扁家族的一連串弊案。這場政治風暴的引爆點始於2005年8月的高捷泰勞抗爭事件，檢方調查揭發高捷公司違法轉包外勞管理以牟取暴利，前總統府副秘書長陳哲男更涉入接受招待與關說疑雲。風暴最終迫使時任高雄市代理市長陳其邁請辭負責，引發民進黨在年底三合一選舉慘敗，而核准高捷興建的時任行政院長謝長廷也隨後引咎下台。

醜聞接連引爆：倒扁浪潮與權力下放

高捷弊案平息不久，陳水扁女婿趙建銘捲入台開內線交易案遭到收押，成為中華民國史上首位被羈押的第一家庭成員。隨後第一夫人吳淑珍的國務機要費案與SOGO禮券案接連引爆，激發了大規模的紅衫軍反貪倒扁運動。接踵而至的貪腐醜聞重創執政聲譽，陳水扁民調跌破兩成，在泛藍陣營發動三次罷免案的壓力下，陳水扁被迫宣布「權力下放」，將憲法以外的職權交由時任行政院長蘇貞昌主導，民進黨陷入泥淖。

藍營聲勢鼎盛與宋楚瑜的政治豪賭

與民進黨的低迷形成強烈對比，國民黨在時任黨主席馬英九的超高人氣帶領下士氣如虹，全力瞄準2008年重返執政，多位黨內菁英亦摩拳擦掌角逐2006年台北市長接班人。然而，在2004年總統大選以微小差距落敗的親民黨主席宋楚瑜，面臨政治光環遭馬英九大幅擠壓、黨內民代紛紛動搖的生存困境。為了避免親民黨在國會與地方基層邊緣化，宋楚瑜於2006年初表態不排除親自參選台北市長，企圖背水一戰以迫使國民黨坐上談判桌。

馬英九祭出條款反制與橘營磁吸效應

面對宋楚瑜參選帶來的變數，國民黨主席馬英九隨即發動反制，祭出「入黨四個月條款」，規定唯有入黨滿四個月者才能登記參選公職。此舉在親民黨內引發強烈的磁吸效應，有意參選台北市長的親民黨立委李慶安等人隨即宣布退黨並重返國民黨，讓原本就處於邊緣化的親民黨面臨更嚴峻的骨牌效應，為後續的泛藍內部整合與台北市長選戰埋下了戲劇性的衝突伏筆。

摘要

政治風暴的前奏：高捷弊案重創綠營執政

作者回顧2006年台北市長選舉前夕的台灣政局，指出當時選民焦點並非市政，而是圍繞在時任總統陳水扁家族的一連串弊案。這場政治風暴的引爆點始於2005年8月的高捷泰勞抗爭事件，檢方調查揭發高捷公司違法轉包外勞管理以牟取暴利，前總統府副秘書長陳哲男更涉入接受招待與關說疑雲。風暴最終迫使時任高雄市代理市長陳其邁請辭負責，引發民進黨在年底三合一選舉慘敗，而核准高捷興建的時任行政院長謝長廷也隨後引咎下台。

高捷弊案平息不久，陳水扁女婿趙建銘捲入台開內線交易案遭到收押，成為中華民國史上首位被羈押的第一家庭成員。隨後第一夫人吳淑珍的國務機要費案與SOGO禮券案接連引爆，激發了大規模的紅衫軍反貪倒扁運動。接踵而至的貪腐醜聞重創執政聲譽，陳水扁民調跌破兩成，在泛藍陣營發動三次罷免案的壓力下，陳水扁被迫宣布「權力下放」，將憲法以外的職權交由時任行政院長蘇貞昌主導，民進黨陷入泥淖。

摘要

政治風暴的前奏：高捷弊案重創綠營執政

作者回顧2006年台北市長選舉前夕的台灣政局，指出當時選民焦點並非市政，而是圍繞在時任總統陳水扁家族的一連串弊案。這場政治風暴的引爆點始於2005年8月的高捷泰勞抗爭事件，檢方調查揭發高捷公司違法轉包外勞管理以牟取暴利，前總統府副秘書長陳哲男更涉入接受招待與關說疑雲。風暴最終迫使時任高雄市代理市長陳其邁請辭負責，引發民進黨在年底三合一選舉慘敗，而核准高捷興建的時任行政院長謝長廷也隨後引咎下台。

醜聞接連引爆：倒扁浪潮與權力下放

高捷弊案平息不久，陳水扁女婿趙建銘捲入台開內線交易案遭到收押，成為中華民國史上首位被羈押的第一家庭成員。隨後第一夫人吳淑珍的國務機要費案與SOGO禮券案接連引爆，激發了大規模的紅衫軍反貪倒扁運動。接踵而至的貪腐醜聞重創執政聲譽，陳水扁民調跌破兩成，在泛藍陣營發動三次罷免案的壓力下，陳水扁被迫宣布「權力下放」，將憲法以外的職權交由時任行政院長蘇貞昌主導，民進黨陷入泥淖。

藍營聲勢鼎盛與宋楚瑜的政治豪賭

與民進黨的低迷形成強烈對比，國民黨在時任黨主席馬英九的超高人氣帶領下士氣如虹，全力瞄準2008年重返執政，多位黨內菁英亦摩拳擦掌角逐2006年台北市長接班人。然而，在2004年總統大選以微小差距落敗的親民黨主席宋楚瑜，面臨政治光環遭馬英九大幅擠壓、黨內民代紛紛動搖的生存困境。為了避免親民黨在國會與地方基層邊緣化，宋楚瑜於2006年初表態不排除親自參選台北市長，企圖背水一戰以迫使國民黨坐上談判桌。

Ma Ying-jeou: if the KMT would step. aside in 2006 to let him be elected. mayor, he would fully support Ma in the. 2008 election and not play the spoiler. But to reach such a deal, the cards. Soong held clearly weren't enough to. move the KMT. After all, succeeding Ma. Ying-jeou as Taipei mayor was an. excellent opportunity for many. Naturally, you wouldn't want the spoils. to go to outsiders. Big names like. Chiang Hsiao-yen—Chiang Wan-an's. father—along with Alex Tsai, and Lee. Ching-an, who had just jumped ship from. the PFP, were all sharpening their. knives, as if passing the primary meant. essentially waiting to take office at. City Hall. But at the time, the. successor Ma Ying-jeou had in mind. wasn't any of these people; it was him. Wait, let's pause right here for a. moment. If you enjoy the content of. this episode, please help us by hitting. subscribe. We will be continuing to. review all eight Taipei mayoral. elections since 1994. Hitting subscribe. is free for you and won't affect your. YouTube homepage algorithm at all, but.

for us, the subscription number is the. most tangible form of encouragement. One person subscribes, one person is. happy; 200,000 subscribe, 200,000 are. happy! Who did I mention earlier that. Ma Ying-jeou preferred? The answer is. his deputy mayor, Yeh Chin-chuan. Yeh. Chin-chuan became famous overnight. during the 2003 SARS outbreak for. single-handedly entering the. locked-down Heping Hospital to provide. support. He was arguably a staff member. Ma relied on heavily during his time as. mayor, and many rumored he would take. up Ma’s mantle to run for mayor. However, just as he was hesitating,. someone else immediately jumped into. the fray: Hau Lung-bin, the son of. military bigwig Hau Pei-tsun. Hau. Lung-bin's political path could be. described as taking quite a long detour. . He left the KMT to serve as a. legislator for the New Party, and in. 2001, he even crossed party lines to. join Chen Shui-bian's cabinet as the. Environmental Protection Administration. minister. During his tenure as EPA. minister, he achieved decent approval. ratings. Although his ideology was at. odds with the DPP, he wasn't exactly. disliked by supporters of the Green. camp at the time. However, it was. precisely because he served in the Chen. Shui-bian administration that many. die-hard deep-blue supporters. questioned this period of Hau. Lung-bin's career, believing he wasn't. "politically correct" and that he even. rode the "April Provisions" back into. the KMT. Before that, he was even a. member of the New Party. Although his. level of loyalty made many people. uneasy, as soon as his father, Hau. Pei-tsun, stepped in, these people. basically had to shut up. After all,. once his background—former Premier,. General of the Army, and even a thorn. in Lee Teng-hui's side—was brought. out, winning over these deep-blue. supporters was an absolute breeze. In. January 2006, Hau Lung-bin announced. his bid for Taipei Mayor. Two days. later, Ma Ying-jeou's deputy mayor, Yeh. Chin-chuan, immediately followed suit,. joined by Ting Shou-chung, representing. Lien Chan's faction. The KMT's primary. race was finally set with just these. three candidates. However, since Ma. Ying-jeou was not only the Mayor of. Taipei but also the KMT Chairman at the. time, Yeh Chin-chuan's close. relationship with him immediately. sparked concerns about a conflict of. interest and whether the primary would. be unfair. Yeh Chin-chuan's camp seemed. pressured by Hau Lung-bin, frequently. attacking him with negative propaganda. and even taking out newspaper ads. mocking him as a "political chameleon." Yes, the term now used to mock many. politicians for changing their stance. originated with Yeh Chin-chuan. Yeh. Chin-chuan's attacks on his own party. members during the primary not only. failed to gain Ma's support, but. actually led to him being quickly. distanced by Ma. Ma even issued a. formal written warning to Yeh through. the party system, which left him. disheartened, leading him to withdraw. just as the primary was moving toward. member voting and polling. After Yeh. Chin-chuan withdrew, Hau Lung-bin. eventually defeated Ting Shou-chung in. the primary, successfully representing. the KMT in the 2006 Taipei Mayoral. election. As for Ting Shou-chung, it. was his third failed attempt at the. primary—a tragic outcome indeed. The. script on the DPP side was completely. the opposite. While the KMT was. fighting over the nomination, nobody in. the DPP wanted to touch it. At the time. , only one former legislator stepped up. : the well-known veteran Shen Fu-hsiung. . But Shen was known within the party. as a "lone bird" with no factional. support; even the Taipei City branch. publicly opposed his candidacy. At the. very last moment before the DPP primary. registration deadline, and under strong. pressure from party leadership to step.

down, Shen Fu-hsiung announced he would. pick up the forms but not register,. leaving behind only one sentence: " Please have the party center draft the. 'first team' to run." Who was the " first team"? The answer is Frank Hsieh,. who had just left his post as Premier. Although the Kaohsiung MRT scandal in. 2005 cast doubt on Frank Hsieh, his. overall governance in Kaohsiung City. was highly regarded. In particular, his. successful cleanup of the Love River. and improvements to water quality in. the Greater Kaohsiung area were truly. his signature achievements. Since Hsieh. is originally from Dadaocheng, running. in Taipei could be considered a natural. progression. The battle ahead was. extremely difficult. In the 1994. primary, Frank Hsieh lost to Chen. Shui-bian by a narrow margin, missing. his chance to be Taipei mayor. After 12. years, he finally secured the. opportunity to represent the DPP in the. Taipei mayoral race, but the heaviest. burden on his back was...Lacking the. right timing, favorable geography, and. popular support—where exactly lay. Frank Hsieh’s chance of winning? For. the DPP at the time, there was no room. to retreat. With the vote share hitting. a new low in the previous election,. they could not afford to leave the. ballot empty no matter how difficult it. was. The only path to a breakthrough. was to find someone to split Hau. Lung-bin's votes, and that person was. James Soong, who we mentioned earlier. was poised to run. However, the polls. immediately delivered a heavy blow. According to media polls in September,. Hau Lung-bin led with 50%support, far. ahead of Hsieh's 15%and Soong's 10%. These poll figures had two meanings:. first, that James Soong posed no threat. to Hau Lung-bin; and second, that for. DPP supporters, the social climate at. the time made them hesitant to express. their stance. This meant that Frank. Hsieh's support level could not reflect. the DPP's basic voter base at all. Speaking of the social climate at the. time, what was actually happening? The. answer is the "Million Voices Against. Corruption, Chen Must Go" movement. launched by former DPP Chairman Shih. Ming-teh, better known to everyone as. the Red Shirt Army. The call to oust. Chen was sounded in August, asking. everyone to donate 100 NT dollars. As a. result, small-sum donations to the. anti-Chen movement broke through 110. million NT dollars in a short period. Thus, Shih Ming-teh began launching. large-scale mass movements, staging. sit-ins at Ketagalan Boulevard,. followed by "fluorescent encirclements,. " and finally, on National Day, they. launched the "Siege of the Whole World. " Hundreds of thousands of people in. red shirts marched around Taipei Main. Station, very close to the Bo'ai. Special Zone, in what could be. considered one of the largest mass. movements in Taiwan's history. The main. battlefield for the Red Shirt Army was. Taipei City. All day long, people. throughout the city shouted for Chen. Shui-bian to step down, while. streetlights and utility poles were. plastered with protest stickers. For. the DPP's mayoral candidate at the time. , Frank Hsieh, it was a disastrous. home-field disadvantage. The Hau. Lung-bin camp did not let this street. energy go to waste. He appealed. directly to Taipei citizens, calling on. voters to use their ballots as another. way to protest against Chen Shui-bian,. channeling the anger of the Red Shirt. Army straight into the polling stations. . As for James Soong, just as the Red. Shirt Army's movement reached its. climax, he finally announced his bid. for Taipei mayor, though he did not run. under the People First Party banner,. but rather as an independent. For Soong. , this was a political gamble. He was. betting that deep-blue voters might not. support Hau Lung-bin because he had. served as an official in the Chen. Shui-bian administration, and that they.

would ultimately turn to him, the "old. governor." By running as an independent. , he hoped to preserve room for. integration with the KMT, betting on a. future where the KMT might be willing. to yield to him. To heat up the. election, Soong even claimed this was. the "last battle of his life." He. didn't even set up a fixed campaign. headquarters, instead driving a tour. bus around Taipei to emphasize his " mobile campaign." Strategy. Facing such. a dire electoral disadvantage, how. could Frank Hsieh turn the tables? First, he focused all his fire on. discussions of municipal affairs. When. others tried to attack him with the. Kaohsiung MRT scandal or the Chen. Shui-bian cases, he immediately. countered by throwing out a barrage of. policy proposals to steer the. conversation, the most sensational of. which was "The 2020 Olympics in Taipei. " That’s right, the core of Frank. Hsieh’s 2006 campaign was to have. Taipei City bid to host the 2020. Olympics. The reason he dared to make. such a bold claim was that, during his. term as Mayor of Kaohsiung, he had. secured the hosting rights for the 2009. World Games. Furthermore, Hsieh was a. gymnast while attending Taipei. Municipal High School of Commerce; his. goal in his youth had been to stand on. the Olympic stage, so in a way, this. policy was also about fulfilling a. childhood dream. The Olympic bid policy. might sound absurd now, but from. another perspective, the election. outlook for Frank Hsieh was already. extremely unfavorable at the time. Plus. , the Red Shirt Army movement hadn't. even ended. Without something drastic,. no one would have focused on the Taipei. mayoral race. This predicament was best. highlighted in early November 2006,. just a month before the election, when. prosecutors indicted First Lady Wu. Shu-chen for allegedly misappropriating. state affairs funds. Although Mayor Ma. Ying-jeou was simultaneously being. investigated by prosecutors for using. his mayoral special allowance to raise. his dog, Ma Hsiao-chiu, the indictment. of Wu Shu-chen was a crushing blow to a. DPP that was already facing strong. headwinds. When Wu Shu-chen was. indicted, the morale within the DPP hit. rock bottom, with some even calling for. Hsieh to suspend his campaign. activities and drop out of the race. entirely. However, Frank Hsieh. continued to hold his Olympic bid. carnival parade as planned, seemingly. completely unaffected by the legal. proceedings. He stated that he was the. party’s nominee and had a. responsibility to the party, so. everything should proceed as usual. For. Frank Hsieh, the way to gently distance. himself from a party central leadership. in turmoil—without triggering a. backlash from pan-green supporters—. was to find ways to create new topics. Beyond offering policy "beef," he. aggressively attacked the privilege. controversies surrounding Hau. Lung-bin’s father, Hau Pei-tsun, and. the Lafayette frigate procurement. scandal associated with him. As for Hau. Lung-bin, he maintained a relatively. low profile since announcing his. candidacy. Beyond the fact that the Red. Shirt Army movement dominated the. headlines, his stable polling numbers. were a key factor. His policy platform. aligned with his past experience as. head of the EPA: to clean up the Tamsui. River and transform it into a fishable,. clear waterway within four years. Furthermore, he aimed to introduce. low-emission buses to reduce Taipei’s. air pollution by ten percent each year. However, as this election reached its. final stages, the level of discussion. still had little to do with policy and. instead revolved around "abandoning one. candidate to save another." The James. Soong camp repeatedly called to " abandon Hau to save Soong," but the. polls never gave him any face. According to Era News 'polling figures.

at the end of November, Hau Lung-bin. held 40.9%, Frank Hsieh had 20.3%, and. James Soong was left with only 7.6%. For a party that once had three. legislative seats and a highly popular. political figure who was a. vice-presidential candidate just a year. prior, these numbers were a harsh. reality check for the third force. However, a dramatic event occurred one. week before the election. Late one. night in early December, Ma Ying-jeou. and James Soong held a four-hour secret. meeting, and news of this soon leaked. out. The Blue camp was in an uproar. over Ma and Soong's clandestine meeting. , especially the Hau Lung-bin camp, as. it seemed to validate Soong's claim: " Soong to City Hall, Ma to the. Presidential Office." This meeting. threatened to create a massive upset in. the final stretch, causing Blue. supporters and Ma fans who had already. committed to Hau to begin wavering. Following the news of the Ma-Soong. meeting, rumors spread rapidly, and. banners even appeared on the streets of. Taipei calling for "Ma and Soong to be. sent [to office]." Opponent Frank Hsieh. did not miss this opportunity, joining. in to praise James Soong, hoping that. the more votes Soong siphoned off, the. more he would benefit as the third. party. Would the election results. create the big surprise that both Hsieh. and Soong were hoping for? On December. 9th, the final vote count showed Hau. Lung-bin winning 690,000 votes, a 53%. vote share, while Frank Hsieh received. 520,000 votes. This amounted to a 41%. vote share. As for the much-discussed. James Soong, he only secured over. 53,000 votes, a mere 4%of the total. There were three other candidates in. this election: Li Ao, Ko Ssu-hai, and. the TSU-nominated Jaw Shaw-kong. Although all three were highly. controversial figures, their combined. vote share totaled less than two. percentage points. Regarding voter. turnout, as mentioned at the beginning,. the lack of intensity in the race led. to a record low of only 64%. The Blue. camp felt victory was certain and. didn't bother to vote, while the Green. camp was somewhat affected by the Chen. Shui-bian scandal and the subsequent. anti-Chen sentiment, leaving supporters. with little motivation to head to the. polls. However, Frank Hsieh's vote. share surprised many political. commentators at the time. Polls from. various organizations had consistently. shown him struggling to break 30%, and. many questioned whether he could even. hold the 36%defensive line set by Lee. Ying-yuan in 2002 given the strong. headwinds. In the end, Frank Hsieh's. vote share not only brought the Green. camp's base back to 40%, but he also. received nearly 40,000 more votes than. Lee Ying-yuan had. This defeat, however. , actually paved the way for his 2008. presidential bid. But that year, facing. Ma Ying-jeou, the outcome was not. exactly great either. As for the winner. Hau Lung-bin, on the night of his. victory, he handed the flowers to his. father in the crowd and said, " Reporting to the commander, we have. taken the hill." This allowed the. Kuomintang to surpass the eight-year. mark of governing Taipei City and move. on to the next term. As for James Soong. , the imagined grand endorsement never. happened; Pan-Blue voters ruthlessly. gave the veteran leader an embarrassing. end, causing Soong to announce his. withdrawal from politics immediately. upon his defeat, while the People First. Party's seats in the Taipei City. Council also shrank to just two. The. true historical significance of this. election lies in the fact that it. proved that even during the worst times. of the Red Shirt Army protests and the. "annexation" of news scandals, the Blue. and Green bases remained as stable as. Mount Tai, while the third force was. completely squeezed out of existence. under the extreme polarization of the. Blue and Green camps, eventually.

garnering only 4%of the vote. Do you. still have any impressions of this. Taipei mayoral election from 2006 that. everyone has almost forgotten? Feel. free to leave a comment below and help. make the story more complete.

值得閱讀的理由

  • 深刻剖析台灣1980至1990年代泡沫經濟狂潮下，兩大傳奇「暴發戶」唐日榮與黃任中的崛起歷程與極致奢華的人生百態。
  • 生動還原荒誕卻真實的金錢遊戲：從自稱軍火商的「選美皇帝」純金排場，到科技先鋒轉身成為操盤數十億的「股市大戶金主」。
  • 借古鑑今，透過兩位風雲人物晚年資產散盡、官司纏身的悲劇結局，揭示財富、權力與欲望交織下的深刻警示。

摘要

時代狂潮下的兩大「暴發戶」縮影

作者指出，「暴發戶」在學術定義上指在極短時間內累積巨額財富並以俗氣方式炫富的人。1980至1990年代的台灣迎來泡沫經濟，熱錢湧入、新台幣大幅升值，社會瀰漫著揮金如土的狂熱氣氛。在那個金錢淹腳目的時代，唐日榮與黃任中成為最具話題性的暴發戶象徵。兩人背景與炫富手法截然不同，卻同樣熱愛美女環繞，且晚年皆落入極其悲涼的境地：唐日榮晚年窮困潦倒，身故時資產僅剩七千元新台幣；黃任中則淪為巨額欠稅大戶，遭法院查封拍賣的名貴古董字畫更全被證實為贗品。

從赤貧補教老師到揮金如土的「選美皇帝」唐日榮

唐日榮生於1940年，隨父親遷台後曾是一名貧困的補習班英文老師，過著連牛肉麵都吃不起的生活。1970年代他跨足中東貿易，自稱在留英期間結識薩達姆，並於兩伊戰爭期間擔任「中東軍火商」累積暴利；儘管外界推測其第一桶金實源於紡織配額，但在浮躁社會中無人深究真假。1985年起，唐日榮展開鋪張的炫富大秀：打造純金名片、價值450萬的純金麻將、購入連轉彎都困難的超長型勞斯萊斯並聘請數十名保鑣。1987年他創辦中華民國選美協會並自封「選美皇帝」，身穿特製大元帥禮服，在自家龍椅上檢閱比基尼佳麗；即便因踩踏珍稀動物標本遭國際抨擊，他仍狂妄地將動物皮毛全換成純金雕塑反擊。

權貴之後轉型科技先鋒與「股市金主」黃任中

另一位主角黃任中同樣出生於1940年，為國民黨元老黃少谷的獨子。年少叛逆、曾被列入不良少年名冊的他，赴美接受嚴格軍校教育後返台創業。抱持著「政治太髒、金錢最乾淨」的想法，他從小規模電視維修廠做起，逐步發展為大型電子裝配廠，並成功引進美商RCA在台設立電路板工廠，奠定台灣電子產業擺脫日本技術壟斷的基礎。1984年底，黃任中以每股17.5元買進遠東航空股票，耐心等待十年後以每股225元售出，狂賺56億新台幣，躍居全球華人富豪榜。坐擁龐大資本的他隨即轉身成為幕後巨擘，大方資助雷伯龍、榮安邱等股市四大天王，成為呼風喚雨的「股市大戶製造機」。

================================================

When it comes to the term "nouveau. riche," the academic definition refers. to people who become wealthy in a very. short period of time. In a way, it’s. a term with classist undertones,. implying that you may have started from. a lower social class, but after gaining. unimaginable wealth, you start showing. off in tacky ways. If you use Chinese. slang to describe it, that would be " tuhao." However, I personally believe. that being "tacky" has nothing to do. with social class; for example, look at. our U.S. President. For Taiwanese. people, who are the "nouveau riche" figures that left a deep impression on. you? Today, we are going to introduce. two gentlemen who rose to prominence in. the 1980s, an era of rapid wealth. accumulation in Taiwan. By the 1990s,. their various flamboyant displays made. headlines, making them the talk of that. decade. These two individuals are Tang. Jih-jung and Huang Jen-chung. Their. backgrounds and ways of showing off. were completely different, but they had. one thing in common: they both loved. beautiful women and were always. surrounded by them. Furthermore, in. their later years, they both met the. same tragic fate. One ended up. destitute, passing away with only 7,000. NT dollars in assets and his family. gone. The other became a major tax. delinquent, with nearly all his. property seized; most pitifully, it was. only after the court seized his. valuable antique paintings that they. discovered they were all forgeries. These two famous Taiwanese "nouveau. riche" figures were essentially the. embodiment of the 1990s bubble economy. How exactly did they rise to power, how. do they define the term "nouveau riche,. " and why did they end up in such bleak. circumstances? Hi, this is Xiao Niu. Welcome to "Xiao Niu Talks Finance." To. tell the story of these two "nouveau. riche" figures, we’ll start by. introducing Tang Jih-jung. He was born. in 1940, with his hometown in Chongqing. , China, and came to Taiwan with his. father during the Civil War. After. graduating from university, Tang. Jih-jung's first job was as an English. teacher at a cram school. He once told. the media how poor he was back then; he. rode a beat-up, constantly breaking. motorcycle to teach, didn't have enough. money for beef noodles—only beef. broth noodles—and lived in a tiny,. cramped room that could only fit a bed,. a desk, and a wardrobe. In the 1970s,. relying on the meager savings he had. built up as a cram school teacher, he. started getting into the Middle East. trade business. The following story. sounds a bit like bragging. He claimed. that while studying in the UK, he met. the future Iraqi president, Saddam. Hussein, and during the Iran-Iraq War,. he handled arms deals for Iraq, calling. himself the "King of the Middle East." All of this was just his own account,. and no one ever verified it. Media. reports later suggested that his first. pot of gold didn't come from Middle. Eastern arms at all, but from textile. export quotas. In short, why did Tang. Ri-rong become wealthy overnight? Looking back now, no one really cared. about the truth of the story. Even back. then, no one questioned whether it was. true or false; the fact that he was. incredibly rich was genuine. People. only cared that he looked wealthy, not. how he actually became wealthy. The. protagonist of our other story, Huang. Ren-zhong, was also born in 1940. Compared to Tang Ri-rong, his family. background was much more prominent—he. was the only son of KMT heavyweight. Huang Shao-gu. Who was Huang Shao-gu? He served as Minister of Foreign. Affairs, Vice Premier of the Executive. Yuan, and eventually President of the. Judicial Yuan, acting as a core advisor. to Chiang Kai-shek. With such a. powerful father to lean on, Huang.

Ren-zhong was headstrong and. domineering from a young age. While. attending night classes at Jianguo High. School, he was constantly getting into. fights and was even put on the Taipei. City Police Department's juvenile. delinquency blacklist. After graduation. , he went to university in the US, but. was expelled for fighting, eventually. transferring to a military academy in. Pennsylvania. It was only under the. strict, militarized education that he. finally settled down to complete his. studies. After Taipei lost diplomatic. recognition in 1971, Huang, citing. patriotic reasons, decided to leave the. US and return to Taiwan. 值得閱讀的理由

  • 生動還原荒誕卻真實的金錢遊戲：從自稱軍火商的「選美皇帝」純金排場，到科技先鋒轉身成為操盤數十億的「股市大戶金主」。
  • 借古鑑今，透過兩位風雲人物晚年資產散盡、官司纏身的悲劇結局，揭示財富、權力與欲望交織下的深刻警示。

摘要

時代狂潮下的兩大「暴發戶」縮影

作者指出，「暴發戶」在學術定義上指在極短時間內累積巨額財富並以俗氣方式炫富的人。1980至1990年代的台灣迎來泡沫經濟，熱錢湧入、新台幣大幅升值，社會瀰漫著揮金如土的狂熱氣氛。在那個金錢淹腳目的時代，唐日榮與黃任中成為最具話題性的暴發戶象徵。兩人背景與炫富手法截然不同，卻同樣熱愛美女環繞，且晚年皆落入極其悲涼的境地：唐日榮晚年窮困潦倒，身故時資產僅剩七千元新台幣；黃任中則淪為巨額欠稅大戶，遭法院查封拍賣的名貴古董字畫更全被證實為贗品。

從赤貧補教老師到揮金如土的「選美皇帝」唐日榮

  • 生動還原荒誕卻真實的金錢遊戲：從自稱軍火商的「選美皇帝」純金排場，到科技先鋒轉身成為操盤數十億的「股市大戶金主」。
  • 借古鑑今，透過兩位風雲人物晚年資產散盡、官司纏身的悲劇結局，揭示財富、權力與欲望交織下的深刻警示。

摘要

時代狂潮下的兩大「暴發戶」縮影

作者指出，「暴發戶」在學術定義上指在極短時間內累積巨額財富並以俗氣方式炫富的人。1980至1990年代的台灣迎來泡沫經濟，熱錢湧入、新台幣大幅升值，社會瀰漫著揮金如土的狂熱氣氛。在那個金錢淹腳目的時代，唐日榮與黃任中成為最具話題性的暴發戶象徵。兩人背景與炫富手法截然不同，卻同樣熱愛美女環繞，且晚年皆落入極其悲涼的境地：唐日榮晚年窮困潦倒，身故時資產僅剩七千元新台幣；黃任中則淪為巨額欠稅大戶，遭法院查封拍賣的名貴古董字畫更全被證實為贗品。

從赤貧補教老師到揮金如土的「選美皇帝」唐日榮

唐日榮生於1940年，隨父親遷台後曾是一名貧困的補習班英文老師，過著連牛肉麵都吃不起的生活。1970年代他跨足中東貿易，自稱在留英期間結識薩達姆，並於兩伊戰爭期間擔任「中東軍火商」累積暴利；儘管外界推測其第一桶金實源於紡織配額，但在浮躁社會中無人深究真假。1985年起，唐日榮展開鋪張的炫富大秀：打造純金名片、價值450萬的純金麻將、購入連轉彎都困難的超長型勞斯萊斯並聘請數十名保鑣。1987年他創辦中華民國選美協會並自封「選美皇帝」，身穿特製大元帥禮服，在自家龍椅上檢閱比基尼佳麗；即便因踩踏珍稀動物標本遭國際抨擊，他仍狂妄地將動物皮毛全換成純金雕塑反擊。

權貴之後轉型科技先鋒與「股市金主」黃任中

另一位主角黃任中同樣出生於1940年，為國民黨元老黃少谷的獨子。年少叛逆、曾被列入不良少年名冊的他，赴美接受嚴格軍校教育後返台創業。抱持著「政治太髒、金錢最乾淨」的想法，他從小規模電視維修廠做起，逐步發展為大型電子裝配廠，並成功引進美商RCA在台設立電路板工廠，奠定台灣電子產業擺脫日本技術壟斷的基礎。1984年底，黃任中以每股17.5元買進遠東航空股票，耐心等待十年後以每股225元售出，狂賺56億新台幣，躍居全球華人富豪榜。坐擁龐大資本的他隨即轉身成為幕後巨擘，大方資助雷伯龍、榮安邱等股市四大天王，成為呼風喚雨的「股市大戶製造機」。
